_comment: PROPOSED basal schedule (local clock, units U/hr). NOT applied to the live Nightscout profile. Evidence-based redesign calibrated to Loop's actual delivered basal (see REPORT.md section 11). Phased rollout recommended. Apply only via care-team / Loop workflow.

basal_step1._desc: Step 1 (applied to Loop 2026-06-13 06:48 UTC): overnight cut + midday trough + late-dinner taper.
basal_step1._night1_result: First night overshot to HIGHS overnight: mean 156, max 214, 17% >180, 0% lows. Rise tracked the 22:30 taper (118->157). Midday trough worked well (today 11:00-13:00 ran 83-119, no lows). Conclusion: evening taper too deep; deep-overnight cut was fine. See basal_step1b.

basal_step1b._desc: Step 1b (applied to Loop 2026-06-13 23:25 UTC): walk back evening/overnight cut, keep midday trough.
basal_step1b._week_result: 7-day result (Jun 14-20) vs 90d baseline. NOTE: Jun 17 was sensor day-1 (Dexcom started Jun 16 16:32) and read jumpy-low (29% lows, min 45) - excluded below. EXCL sensor day-1: OVERNIGHT 00-04 SOLVED (%<70 3.1, %<54 0.3, TIR 96.9 - better than goal). Evening fine (%<70 5.4, %<54 0.8) - the low creep was sensor noise, leave it. Dawn 04-07 lows REAL (%<70 9.7, not sensor) -> Step-1c cuts dawn. Midday 11-16 lows REAL (%<70 14.9) and rose despite basal cut => meal/bolus-driven, review lunch carb-ratio. Overall %<70 8.6 / %<54 0.4.

basal_step1c._desc: Step 1c (applied to Loop 2026-06-20 21:33 UTC): cut dawn 04:30 1.55->1.35.
basal_step1c._result: Reviewed Jul 4 (14d, incl. G6->G7 swap Jun 26; G7 warmup auto-excluded). G7 reads same level as G6 (mean 108 vs 110) so comparisons valid. Dawn FIXED (9.7->5.6% <70). Midday improved a lot (15->7.3%, real not calibration). Overnight up to 6.4% but all shallow (nadir 61-67, 0% <54) and partly G7 compression lows -> HOLD basal, don't chase. Severe lows 0.0-0.4% everywhere; excellent control. Verdict: Step-1c is a keeper; hold and watch overnight (behavioral/sensor-placement fix for compression, not basal).

basal_step2._desc: Step 2 (after ~1 week confirming step 1): trim the daytime shoulders (09:30 and merge 16:00-20:00). Merges the old 16:00/17:00 boundaries into one 1.45 afternoon block.

basal_step1d._desc: Step 1d (proposed, LOW PRIORITY - evidence weakened on review): 09:30 1.80 -> 1.45. See _evidence and _revision.
basal_step1d._evidence: 45d review (Jun 9-Jul 24), morning window. FINDING: there is effectively no breakfast - only 35% of days have a >=15g morning carb entry and median first food is 11:18am; the 4/6/8am small entries are corrections at BG~200, not meals. Early morning 04:00-09:00 is GOOD (median 108->118, modest +10 dawn rise, ~0-4% lows, ~0-3% highs) - do not touch. The problem is the LATE-MORNING FASTING SAG: on days with no food before 11:00, 14/16 drifted down, median -16 mg/dL (worst -40/-36/-69), 31% dipped <70, arriving at the first meal already low. Cause: the schedule jumps to 1.80 U/hr at 09:30 (highest daytime rate) mid-fast - apparently vestigial coverage for a breakfast no longer eaten. Loop fights it: hour 10 delivers 1.24 vs 1.80 scheduled, 25% suspended (hr 11: 0.81 vs 1.25, 29% suspended). Morning is the cleanest window for analysis (~0.2 Afrezza-like drops/wk, few fake carbs), so this is fasting-grade evidence.
basal_step1d._revision: REVISED after learning the subject is SLEEPING IN (summer). The 09:00-11:30 window is therefore still SLEEP, not a daytime fast, so the same G7 compression that inflates overnight lows also applies here (lying on the sensor). Re-running with compression episodes excluded: median fasting drift shrinks from -16 to -9 mg/dL (11/12 days still fall, so direction is robust but magnitude halved), and %<70 in 09:00-11:30 falls to ~0-4% (the '31% dipped <70' was largely artifact). The 'Loop is suspending 25%' signal is also partly circular - compression lows cause Loop to suspend. Landing at ~96-101 before the first meal is acceptable. VERDICT: the 09:30 bump is still anomalous but the case for changing it is weak and the pattern is SEASONAL (will shift when school resumes). Prefer to hold, or use a Loop Override on sleep-in days rather than editing the permanent schedule.

first_meal_review_2026_07_24._desc: First-meal-of-day analysis (the real 'breakfast', ~12:18 due to summer sleep-in). The best-supported meal-side finding to date, because the morning window is comparatively free of unlogged Afrezza (~0.2/wk) and fake carbs (>=25g filter).
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._finding: Strongly asymmetric: 22% of first meals dip <70 within 4h vs only 2% peaking >180, with median peak just 135. The dose is a touch strong for the starting point - he arrives at ~89 already drifting down, then boluses at an effective CR of 5.7 (stronger than the profile's 6).
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._option: Weaken the first-meal carb ratio in the window he actually eats (currently ~10:00-15:00): CR 6 -> 7. A 50g meal would take ~7.1U instead of ~8.3U (~1.2U less, ~60 mg/dL at ISF 53). Expected: most of the 22% lows resolve; peak rises from ~135 toward ~150-160, still well under 180. SEASONAL CAVEAT: the window is tied to the summer sleep-in and will need revisiting when the schedule shifts.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._caution: Single-variable discipline: do NOT combine with a basal change. ISF stays unvalidated (corrections are mostly invisible Afrezza/fake-carb).
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._meal_taxonomy: CORRECTED: the first meal of the day is always BREAKFAST regardless of clock time (subject sleeps in; summer). Sometimes there is no lunch, or only a snack. Analysis is therefore by meal ORDINAL, not clock hour. Breakfast n=45 median 12:15 (IQR 11:48-12:54); mid-meal/snack n=23 median 15:38; dinner n=41 median 19:27.

breakfast.read: over-insulinized relative to need: 22% low vs 4% high, peak only 133

mid_meal_snack.read: chaotic both directions; small n and sits in the dinner-time Afrezza window - DO NOT TUNE

dinner.read: balanced 17/17 - leave alone; already effectively dosed weaker than breakfast

first_meal_review_2026_07_24._two_wave_finding: KEY. Post-breakfast median trajectory shows TWO low waves, not one: (a) an EARLY dip at 30-90min (BG 89 -> 84 at 30min; 16% <70 at 60min) - the prebolus acting before the food, from an already-low start; and (b) a LATE wave at 240-270min (13-16% <70) - the insulin tail. Median time from breakfast to first <70 is 80 min (IQR 60-230), so the EARLY dip dominates. The meal does not peak until ~180min and only reaches 136. Interpretation: this is primarily a STARTING-BG + PREBOLUS-TIMING problem, not purely carb ratio.
_options_ranked: 1. BEHAVIORAL (zero settings risk, targets the dominant 30-90min dip): when pre-breakfast BG is <90 and flat/falling, skip or shorten the prebolus - bolus at first bite instead.

2. BASAL (passive, no behavior change needed): Step-1d 09:30 1.80 -> 1.45 now has a better rationale - not the -9 drift itself, but arriving at breakfast nearer 98-100 instead of 89 gives the prebolus dip headroom before it crosses 70.
3. CARB RATIO (targets the late 240-270min wave): breakfast-window CR 6 -> 6.5 (~8%, standard increment). CR 7 is the more decisive test given peak is only 133, but 6.5 is the by-the-book first step.
Do ONE at a time. Dinner and mid-meal should not be changed.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._seasonal: All of this is tied to the summer sleep-in: breakfast is currently ~12:15. When school resumes, breakfast moves earlier and any time-windowed CR segment (and the 09:30 basal rationale) must be revisited.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._CORRECTION: METHODOLOGICAL ERROR in the first pass, now fixed. Peaks were measured in a 2.5h window, but breakfast does not peak until ~3h, so the peak was TRUNCATED and highs under-reported. Corrected 5h window (n=45): median peak 165 (not 133), 29% exceed 180 (not 4%), 51% dip below 70, and 16% do BOTH within the same meal; only 36% are clean. CONCLUSION REVERSED: breakfast swings both ways - it is NOT simply over-insulinized, so weakening the carb ratio is the WRONG fix (it would worsen the 29% highs). The problem is shape/timing, not dose magnitude.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._behavioral_rule_test: The proposed rule 'pre-BG <95 and flat/falling -> skip prebolus' does NOT discriminate: risky group 35% dip <70 within 2h vs 32% for all others (n=17 vs 28). Trend direction ran backwards from expectation (falling 22% early-dip vs flat 50%, rising 39%) - noise at this n. The ONLY surviving signal is the starting level: pre-BG <80 -> 60% dip <70 (n=10) vs 22-38% for all higher bands.
first_meal_review_2026_07_24._recommendation_2026_07: HOLD ALL SETTINGS. (1) The data cannot support a confident breakfast change - both-ways swing, no clean threshold. (2) The pattern is tied to the summer sleep-in (12:15 breakfast) and is about to be erased by travel and then a college dorm. (3) A change made now would be evaluated during travel, the noisiest possible baseline. Keep Step-1c (holding well: TIR 93%, GMI 5.9%). Carry ONE portable, BG-triggered rule that survives time zones and a shifting class schedule: do not take a full meal bolus starting under 80 - eat the first bites first or bring BG up before dosing. Re-assess 2-3 weeks into the dorm once a routine exists. NOTE: user correctly ruled out a time-of-day basal segment for the morning - first class varies by day, so a clock-based fix cannot work.

pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._desc: POD-CYCLE (3-day Omnipod) EFFECT - user hypothesis, confirmed. Largest single systematic driver of variability found to date, and the only intervention that is schedule-independent (anchored to pod changes, not the clock).
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._data: 45d, 19 site changes, median pod life 2.5d (two <1d = likely failures). Bolus insulin is FLAT across pod days (43.1/43.8/43.8 U/day) so this is an ABSORPTION effect, not a dosing difference.
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._robustness: Gradient holds in EVERY time-of-day window after excluding G7 compression (%<70 day1/2/3): night 3.7/0.2/0.6, morning 6.4/4.2/1.4, afternoon 10.4/6.8/4.0, evening 9.3/5.0/3.9. Mean glucose rises monotonically with pod age in every window. Not a time-of-day artifact - pod changes cluster in the afternoon/evening but the effect survives matching on time of day.

_breakfast_by_pod_day.note: Explains the previously confusing 'breakfast swings both ways' result: the highs are concentrated on pod day 3 (peak +37 vs day 1, 55% >180), the lows on day 1. Two distinct problems that averaged into one. Low side is noisier at this n (44/69/36) - the peak/high gradient is the clean signal.

pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._direction: Fresh site absorbs BETTER (more insulin action -> lows on day 1); absorption degrades with pod age (less action -> highs on day 3). Note this is the OPPOSITE of what a naive 'day 1 is erratic' expectation predicts, and the magnitude (mean 105 -> 118, lows 7.4% -> 2.5%) is comparable to the entire basal retune.
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._why_it_fits_the_constraints: Anchored to pod changes (~every 2.5d), NOT the clock. Survives travel, time zones, a college dorm, and a class schedule that differs by day - precisely where a time-of-day basal segment fails.
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._option: A pod-day-aware Loop Override pair: a gentler-insulin override for roughly the first 12-24h after a pod change (to cut the day-1 lows) and/or a stronger one for the last ~12h before a change (to cut the day-3 highs). Loop overrides scale basal/ISF/CR together and can be time-limited. MAGNITUDE NOT ESTABLISHED HERE - start conservative (~5-10%) and set with the care team; do not derive the percentage from these aggregates.
pod_cycle_finding_2026_07._caveats: Breakfast-by-pod-day cells are small (n=11-16). The overall gradient is robust (n=2731-4999/day). Two sub-1-day pod gaps (failures) were left in. Site-change events are user-logged; an unlogged change would blur the boundaries.

basal_step2_2026_08._desc: Step 2 (proposed 2026-08-23): flatten the two vestigial daytime bumps AND scale ~15%. 38.05 -> 31.73 U/day (-17%), 9 segments -> 7.
basal_step2_2026_08._rationale: PRIMARY JUSTIFICATION IS THE DELIVERED-VS-SCHEDULED GAP, NOT ANY TIME-OF-DAY OUTCOME. Loop delivers ~24.5 U/day on late-start days and ~20.4 on early-start days against a scheduled 38.05 - the schedule is 56% above actual delivery, and Loop suspends 30-40% of the time routinely (up to 74% in some hours). Two consequences: (1) FAILURE MODE - the scheduled basal is what the pod falls back to if Loop stops (phone dead, lost comms, app crash), i.e. a 56% over-delivery scenario, potentially overnight, while he is unsupervised in a dorm; (2) NO HEADROOM - Loop spends most of its control range holding the baseline down instead of responding to real lows. The two flattened bumps (09:30 1.80, 16:00 1.80) are rejected by Loop on EVERY day type (delivers 1.27/0.83 and 0.99/0.65, suspending 24-62%), so removing them is robust to schedule changes. In a closed loop, meal coverage should come from the bolus, not a standing basal bump.
basal_step2_2026_08._expected_effect: Should NOT materially change delivered insulin - Loop will simply suspend less to reach the same targets. This is a safety/headroom change, NOT a fix for the current hypoglycemia. Risk of lowering is correspondingly low precisely because Loop is already ignoring the schedule. New schedule still sits ~29% above Loop's late-day delivery.
basal_step2_2026_08._does_not_fix: The recurrent lows. Loop is already delivering only 20.4 U/day on active days and still going low, so the driver is elsewhere (activity + meal/bolus, likely the early-breakfast response: peak 137-155 at 08-09 then 14-18% <54 at 10-12).
basal_step2_2026_08._sample_caveat: IMPORTANT. The 'early-start' days in this analysis (n=7, first meal <9am) were BAND CAMP (Aug 10-14) plus a Saturday band event (Aug 22) - NOT the coming semester. The 'late-start' days (n=52) were the summer sleep-in. Neither group represents the expected routine (first class ~9am). All ACTIVITY-SPECIFIC conclusions (the 10:00-12:00 cluster, override timing, the overnight tail) are therefore fitted to a transient week and must be re-derived after a few weeks of real semester data. The delivered-vs-scheduled gap above is schedule-independent and does survive.

_alternatives.B_proportional_15: 32.31 U (-15%): scale only, keep all 9 segments

basal_step2_2026_08._next: Do NOT pair this with an activity override in the same step - one variable at a time. Re-derive activity handling once the ~9am-class pattern has a few weeks of data.

basal_overnight_2026_08_23._desc: APPLIED to Loop 2026-08-23 23:09 UTC (16:09 local) and verified against the uploaded profile. Overnight-only reduction; daytime, targets, ISF and CR all untouched.
basal_overnight_2026_08_23._rationale: Loop was delivering ~24.5 U/day against 38.05 scheduled (56% above), suspending 27-38% of overnight hours. Two aims: (1) reduce real overnight delivery - during the ~65% of the night Loop is not suspended, a lower baseline means less insulin; (2) fix the failure mode, since the scheduled rate is what the pod reverts to if Loop stops, which matters now he is unsupervised in a dorm. 04:30-09:30 deliberately left at 1.35 - the one block Loop accepts (delivers 1.00-1.11, suspends only 10-16%, produces no lows); cutting it is the change most likely to create morning highs that get over-corrected.
basal_overnight_2026_08_23._watch: WORKING: overnight 00:00-05:00 %<54 toward <1%, no nadir under 60, morning 07:00-09:00 mean stays under ~140. TOO FAR: morning mean past ~160 or morning corrections appear -> back the overnight rates up halfway. NOT ENOUGH: severe lows persist 00:00-05:00 after 5-7 clean nights -> second step 1.55/1.10/0.90. IGNORE single bad nights and the first 24h of any new sensor.
basal_overnight_2026_08_23._baseline_to_beat: Prior 2 weeks: %<54 1.8-3.1% overall; overnight nadirs 40, 43, 50. Late-start days ran 0.9% <54, early-start days 4.0%.
basal_overnight_2026_08_23._confound_warning: Late-correction rules (no manual correction under ~150 after 10pm; Afrezza instead of subcutaneous; no Rage/fake carbs at night) may be adopted in the same window. If so the two changes are entangled and neither can be cleanly attributed - note which nights had late manual corrections when reviewing.
basal_overnight_2026_08_23._first_night: 2026-08-23 (applied 16:09 local, so tonight is the first night on the new schedule).

basal_afternoon_2026_09_05._desc: PROPOSED 2026-09-05: afternoon-only trim. 09:30 1.80->1.50, 11:00 1.25->0.95, 16:00 1.80->1.40. Evening (17:00/18:00), overnight, dawn and dinner blocks all UNCHANGED. 35.35 -> 33.00 U/day (-7%).
basal_afternoon_2026_09_05._week_review: 7 days on the Aug 28 changes (18:00 1.35 + maximumBolus 10->15). WORKED: overnight 00-05 severe lows held at 0.0%; morning improved; post-dinner improved (8.1->2.0% <70). MAX BOLUS used as intended - 6 boluses >10U (~4.7/wk), max 15.00 twice, cap-pinning at exactly 10.00 fell from 14 to 1, manual boluses dropped ~12.4/day to ~8/day. Total bolus 48.8 -> 38.5 U/day with carbs 219 -> 172 g/day. DID NOT WORK: afternoon deteriorated badly - 11:00-20:00 now runs 12-26% <70 every hour, worst at 14:00 (Loop suspends 68%, delivers 0.37 vs 1.25 scheduled, 25.6% <70, 10.3% <54). Overall %<70 7.0 -> 10.1 though %<54 edged down 1.8 -> 1.4; mean 111 -> 103. Classes started ~Sep 1.
basal_afternoon_2026_09_05._key_split: WEEKDAY vs WEEKEND separates two different problems. AFTERNOON 11-17 is bad on BOTH (weekday mean 96 / 22.0% <70 / 3.9% <54; weekend mean 86 / 16.5% / 2.3%) - weekend mean is actually LOWER, so this is a background shift, not campus walking, and a basal change is the right tool. EVENING 17-20 is WEEKDAY-ONLY (weekday 25.6% <70, 6.1% <54; weekend 0.0% and 0.0%, mean 110) - that is activity, and a permanent cut there would create weekend evening highs. Hence evening is deliberately left alone and should be handled with an activity override (existing presets: 0.8x/target 120, 0.7x/target 120) on class days.
basal_afternoon_2026_09_05._meal_note: 7 of 7 midday meals post-change were followed by a low. Doses ran effective CR 4.8-6.1 from starting BG 72-89. But Sep 4 was dosed 5.0U for 100g (effective CR 20, a large under-dose) and STILL reached 55 - so the driver is background/activity, not primarily the meal bolus.
basal_afternoon_2026_09_05._rejected_alternative: A broader version also cutting 17:00->1.05 and 18:00->1.05 (31.75 U/day, -10%) was rejected: weekend evenings already run mean 110 with 0% lows, so permanently cutting the evening would create highs on non-class days.
basal_afternoon_2026_09_05._watch: WORKING: afternoon 11-17 %<54 toward <1% and no nadir under 60, while 09:30-11:00 does not drift high. TOO FAR: afternoon mean climbs past ~140 or he starts correcting mid-afternoon. STILL WEEKDAY-ONLY EVENING LOWS: that is the override's job, not basal. CAVEAT: only ~5 days of the new class routine; expect to revisit.
basal_afternoon_2026_09_05._withdrawn_because: Sized against SCHEDULED rates without checking DELIVERED. Aug 29-Sep 4, hours 12-15: Loop suspends 77-84% and delivers 0.13-0.21 U/hr against the 1.25 schedule; hour 18 delivers 0.23 against 1.35. Cutting 1.25->0.95 sits well above actual delivery, so it is close to a no-op: these lows occur with basal ALREADY off. (Second-order only: a suspended basal accrues negative IOB against the scheduled rate, so a lower schedule would soften Loop's downstream dosing — real, but too small to justify the change alone.) Also weakens the original 'weekends are worse -> background shift' argument: Sat 08/29, one of the two weekend days it rested on, has an Activity override logged at 13:33.
basal_afternoon_2026_09_05._next_read: Sun 09/06 + Mon 09/07 (holiday) are low-activity days at UNCHANGED rates — the clean read never yet obtained. Afternoons still 11-25% <70 on a quiet day => driver is meal dosing (CR 6), since basal is already suspended; cf. Sep 4 lunch dosed 5.0U/100g (effective CR 20) and still hit 55. Afternoons clean => campus walking, and the lever is an override on class days, not the schedule.
basal_afternoon_2026_09_05._game_day_note: Sat 09/05 is a game day at Snapdragon. Precedent: the night of Sat 08/22 -> Sun 08/23 ran 10.7% <54, the worst overnight in 21d (every other night 0.0-2.4%); 08/22 is the only event-looking Saturday in the window (300g carbs, 54.5U, overrides from 07:23). Delayed post-activity overnight low. Handle tonight with an activity override started in the evening and carried through the night — not a schedule change.

read_2026_09_07_home_weekend._desc: Sat 09/05 (game day) + Sun 09/06 (rest day) at home. The low-activity read that the withdrawn afternoon basal cut was waiting on. CONFIRMS the withdrawal and relocates the problem from basal to (a) meal-bolus timing on activity days and (b) override strength.
read_2026_09_07_home_weekend._sunday_rest_day: Hours 05-13 and 15-23 all 0.0% <70. The ONLY afternoon low was hour 14 (mean 65, 83.9% <70, 0.0% <54), ~2h after 50g lunch dosed 8.45U at 13:32 (CR 5.9), with basal 100% suspended through it. So afternoon lows are NOT background basal — the schedule is fine on a rest day — but they are also not purely campus walking, since one occurred at home with no walking. Common factor is the meal bolus.
read_2026_09_07_home_weekend._activity_stacks: Midday 11-16 <70: Tue 31.9%, Wed 31.7%, Thu 36.2%, Fri 13.2% (class days) vs Sun 13.3% (rest). Activity adds hours 12/13/15 on top of the post-lunch hour-14 dip that happens regardless.
read_2026_09_07_home_weekend._saturday_night_override_was_run_and_fai: Recommendation was followed: ⬇️ Running Low (x0.80/target 120) ran near-continuously 19:30 -> 01:00 (five back-to-back overrides). BG still hit 51 at 23:15 and 46 at 00:30, needing 40g rescue at 00:10, then a third low 03:00-03:30. x0.80 is too weak for a game day.
read_2026_09_07_home_weekend._the_mechanism: The 80g dinner was bolused 11.85U at 17:09 + 1.05U at 17:35 (~12.9U, CR ~6.2). The override did not start until 19:30 — 2h20m AFTER the dose. A Loop override scales CR and ISF, so it only reduces boluses computed WHILE ACTIVE; it cannot retract insulin already delivered. The largest dose of the evening went out at full strength into a post-exercise sensitivity window. Timing, not just magnitude.
read_2026_09_07_home_weekend._overnight_tracks_prior_day_activity: Fri 09/04 (band) -> that night 31.8% <70. Sat 09/05 (game) -> that night 20.9% <70 / 7.9% <54. Sun 09/06 (rest) -> that night 0.0% <70, mean 119. Delayed post-exercise overnight lows, cleanly separated.
read_2026_09_07_home_weekend._recommendation_2026_09_07: ONE change, phone-side: add an activity preset at x0.65 / target 130 (nothing weaker than x0.80 exists today). Use it differently from Running Low — ON BEFORE the activity and before the meal bolus, left running overnight, rather than switched on after the fall. Saturday's 12.9U dinner would have been ~8.4U. Do NOT change basal: Sunday shows the schedule is correct on a rest day.
read_2026_09_07_home_weekend._not_changing_yet: CR 6. Sunday's hour-14 post-lunch low is one data point at home and points at CR, but one change at a time — and Mon 09/07 is a holiday (low activity, unrepresentative), so the first real test of the preset is Tue 09/08 and the next band/game day.

carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._desc: PROPOSED 2026-09-07: first carb-ratio change of this engagement, and the first time-segmented setting. CR 6 flat -> 7.0 between 10:00 and 16:00; 00:00 and 16:00 segments stay at 6.
carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._why: Midday collapsed across ~Aug 25 at an UNCHANGED dose. Meals >=25g, 30d, median values: midday 10-16 before Aug25 n=17 effCR 6.0 peak 163 nadir 75 0.0% <70; Aug25->now n=15 effCR 5.9 peak 158 nadir 55 14.6% <70. Dinner 16-22 is the control and did not move: 0.0% <70 in BOTH eras (effCR 8.0->7.8, peak 165->183, nadir 72->79). TDD flat across the break (48.9 -> 48.3 U on 172 -> 174 g carbs), so this is not a global sensitivity shift — it is confined to the midday window, which is what a CR segment is for.
carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._sizing: Median midday nadir 55 vs target ~85 = ~0.6U at ISF 53 on a median 8.6U dose. Open-loop that is 8% (CR 6.5); after Loop's measured 1.15U median clawback it needs ~14% (CR 7) to net the same. Expected peak ~158 -> ~175-185, i.e. about where dinner already sits.
carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._staged_next_step: If a week shows highs being chased with Rage, fall back to 6.5. If still >10% <70, go 7.5. Note one meal (Fri 09/04) was dosed at effective CR 20 and still ran 16.7% <70 — beyond what any ratio fixes; that is the activity preset's job, not the CR's.
carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._does_not_replace_the_activity_preset: CR covers the everyday campus routine — the part that must not depend on remembering. It does NOT cover game/band days: Sat 09/05 reached 46 despite a continuously-run x0.80 override, and the post-activity OVERNIGHT lows (Fri 09/04 night 31.8% <70; Sat 09/05 night 20.9% / 7.9% <54; rest-day Sun night 0.0%) follow DINNER, which is in the 16:00 segment left unchanged. Those still need the x0.65/target-130 preset, on before the meal bolus.
carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._compensating_not_correcting: The ratio did not become wrong; the days changed (dorm + classes + marching band from late Aug). This is a seasonal setting. Revisit when band season ends or at semester break, or he will run high.
carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._soft_edge: Start chosen as 10:00 because first meal is now often 10:10-10:48 and those recently went low (10.6%, 12.5%, 29.2% <70). If mornings drift high, move the segment start to 11:00.

carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._revised_6_5_to_7: Initially proposed 6.5 from an open-loop ISF calculation (lift median midday nadir 55 -> ~85 = ~0.6U on a median 8.6U dose = ~8%). That ignored Loop's own counter-action and was under-powered. MEASURED: after midday meals Loop delivers a median 1.15U of AUTOMATIC correction in the 1-5h window (spread 0.40-3.15U, 15% of the meal dose). A 6->6.5 cut removes only 0.66U — smaller than Loop's median clawback and inside its spread, so it would likely be unmeasurable. 6->7 removes 1.23U, the first step that clears that noise. Second-order effect points the same way: a weaker meal dose raises the forecast, so Loop corrects MORE than it did — visible in the split, where meals that stayed up drew 2.05U of auto-correction vs 0.95U for meals that went low. Because Loop opposes the change, the setting must be over-specified to net the intended effect; 7 nets roughly what 6.5 would net open-loop.
carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._why_the_high_side_is_the_cheap_error: Loop has full authority to correct a high — it routinely delivers 2-3U of automatic correction. It has almost no authority to correct a low beyond suspending basal, which it is ALREADY doing 75-84% of the time in hours 12-15. Asymmetric cost, so err weak. CR 7 also still sits BELOW dinner's effective ~8, the window that peaks 183 with zero lows — moving midday toward a validated regime, not past it.
carbratio_midday_2026_09_07._review_plan: First meaningful read is Tue 09/08 — Mon 09/07 is a holiday and unrepresentative. Check three things: (1) do midday nadirs move off a median of 55; (2) do midday peaks stay under ~185, i.e. at or below dinner's current 183; (3) does afternoon Rage usage rise, which is the signal we overshot and should fall back to 6.5. rage_retarget_2026_09_10._desc: PROPOSED 2026-09-10: retarget the 🤬 Rage preset from target 80 to target 100. Multiplier stays x1.20. No other setting touched. Addresses the largest single driver of severe lows found so far.
rage_retarget_2026_09_10._scale_of_the_problem: 140 Rage episodes in 40 days = 3.5/day, median trigger BG 150, median 3.10U manual + 10g fake carbs in the following hour. 43% end <70 within 1-4h and 22% end <54 — roughly 30 severe lows in 40 days downstream of this one habit. Larger than anything basal or CR tuning has addressed.
rage_retarget_2026_09_10._it_is_not_the_dose: Splitting by manual dose (>=3U vs <3U) shows NO difference: nadir 74 vs 76, ended <54 23% vs 20%. The discriminator is the RISE RATE at the moment he reacts.
rage_retarget_2026_09_10._by_rise_rate_30min: falling/flat n=18 -> 28% <70, 11% <54 | slow +5..25 n=45 -> 36%, 13% | fast +25..45 n=60 -> 47%, 22% | VERY FAST 45+ n=13 -> 69% <70, 62% <54 at median BG only 143 and the SMALLEST median dose of any group (2.55U). Confirms the user's description: he reads a steep arrow as an incoming bad high and corrects, but on a fast rise Loop is already dosing hard against the carbs and the manual dose lands in the trough.
rage_retarget_2026_09_10._by_trigger_bg: under 120 n=19 -> 53% <70 / 26% <54 | 120-149 n=47 -> 57% / 30% (his biggest bucket AND the worst outcomes) | 150-179 n=55 -> 24% / 5% (this one works) | 180-219 n=15 -> 47% / 47%. The danger zone is correcting while only mildly elevated but climbing.
rage_retarget_2026_09_10._why_retargeting_has_the_right_shape: Target 80 -> 100 removes a FIXED 20/53 = 0.38U from every Loop-computed correction, which is proportionally large exactly where he gets hurt and small where the tool is warranted: BG ~104 0.45U -> 0.08U (83% smaller); BG ~137 1.08 -> 0.70 (35%); BG ~161 1.53 -> 1.15 (25%); BG ~230 2.82 -> 2.44 (13%). Requires ZERO behavior change — same button, same frequency.
rage_retarget_2026_09_10._why_not_a_behavioral_fix: Asking him not to react to a steep arrow was rejected by the user as unworkable, correctly: the reflex is the stable thing here at 3.5x/day. Change what the button does, not whether he presses it.
rage_retarget_2026_09_10._caveat: Reverse causation is partly present: a very fast rise implies a large fast-carb meal, so meal bolus + Loop auto-correction are already on board and some of those lows would occur regardless. Retargeting removes one contributor. Expect the <54 rate to fall meaningfully, not to zero.
rage_retarget_2026_09_10._next_step_if_insufficient: After ~2 weeks, if still >15% of episodes ending <54, change the multiplier x1.20 -> x1.10. One change at a time.
